items.title: PostgreSQL 18.6 / 17.11 / 16.15 / 15.19 / 14.24 fix 28 CVEs and 110+ bugs — the largest single PostgreSQL security release to date.

CVE-2026-19385 (8.8) turns your backup job into the attack surface: a crafted function transform list overflows a heap buffer in pg_dump and runs code as the OS user doing the dump.
CVE-2026-14663: pgcrypto silently encrypted to/from cleartext when a disabled cipher was requested (CVSS 6.5).
Two quieter auth findings worth a config review — CVE-2026-14672 (5.3): a non-default scram_iterations makes response timing a username-existence oracle; CVE-2026-14681 (4.2): GSSAPI encryption not…
CVE-2026-6464 (8.1) hits the client, not the server: an early COPY FROM STDIN failure makes psql interpret the data lines as psql commands.
CockroachDB v26.3 shipped fixes for multiple privilege-escalation bugs in constraint validation and logical data replication, alongside a new VIEWEVENTLOG privilege for granular DB Console RBAC.
MySQL 9.7.3 (Aug 18) is a Critical Security Patch Update for the Docker image only — no server changelog; details live in Oracle's August 2026 CSPU advisory (which blocks automated fetching).
Parallel GIN index builds wrote garbage reltuples into pg_class (Infinity/NaN), which silently stops autovacuum/autoanalyze on those tables.
REINDEX required for two index classes: btree_gist over float4/float8 columns containing NaN or over bit/bit-varying, and btree over ltree values with >14,653 labels.
A self-deadlock during WAL replay from older minor versions could freeze standbys on 14/15/16 — relevant if you do rolling minor upgrades standby-first, which is most people.
18.5 was skipped entirely due to a regression — if your version pin says 18.5, it does not exist; go to 18.6.
Three headline features were reverted during beta: SQL/PGQ property graphs (Sept 7, 47 commits), ALTER TABLE … MERGE/SPLIT PARTITION (Aug 27, 14 commits), and GROUP BY ALL (in Beta 3).
What survives is the operationally interesting half: REPACK … CONCURRENTLY (online table rewrite without pg_repack), parallel autovacuum, pg_plan_advice, async-I/O worker autoscaling, and logical…
Five incompatibilities to plan for now: JIT is OFF by default, default_toast_compression flips pglz → lz4, RADIUS auth is removed outright, vacuumdb --analyze-only now analyzes partitioned tables…
MD5 authentication now emits deprecation warnings — the countdown on md5 password verifiers has visibly started.
GA is still officially "September/October 2026"; no RC1 as of today.

Spanner changed mutation accounting: the 80,000 limit now applies per DML statement rather than cumulatively per transaction (Aug 11).
Spanner added expression-based secondary indexes (Aug 28), removing the generated-column workaround, plus TABLESAMPLE (Sep 2) and ILIKE/NOT ILIKE (Sep 3) for PG-dialect databases.
